findings.title: [REPLAY] Sensitive access then egress to 127.0.0.1
findings.observed: 2 sensitive-path access(es) (sensitive:ssh) preceded egress to 127.0.0.1 (exec via terminal).
findings.why: Credential material was in reach of the agent immediately before it contacted the outside world.
findings.recommendation: Check whether the destination is one you expect for this task; rotate the credentials named in the evidence if it is not. Add the destination to allow_hosts if this is a routine deploy.
missing_evidence: File contents are never recorded, so whether the credential bytes were in the request body is not visible.
Shell network calls are inferred from command text; the connection itself is not observed.
findings.attack_note: T1700 is attached because the actor is an AI agent; T1567.004 replaces T1567 when the host is a known webhook/paste service.

findings.rule_name: Subagent acted outside its parent's scope
findings.title: [REPLAY] Subagent secret.access outside parent scope: /Users/demo/siemless-lab/.ssh/id_rsa
findings.observed: Child session kid6… did secret.access (/Users/demo/siemless-lab/.ssh/id_rsa); its parent did nothing of the kind in the window.
findings.why: A child agent's goal is a brief from the parent; a sensitive action the parent never took is privilege propagation.
findings.recommendation: Read the child's goal (subagent.start) and its tool history (subagent.stop) in the evidence.
missing_evidence: Child tool history is metadata-only by Hermes design: tool names and bounded targets, no arguments.
findings.attack_note: Delegation itself is not a technique; the finding carries the child's action's mapping via SL-001/003.

findings.title: [REPLAY] Credential store targeted: /Users/demo/siemless-lab/.ssh/id_rsa
findings.why: Credential stores are rarely needed for ordinary tasks; each access is worth a glance, and it is the first step of SL-001.
findings.recommendation: If the task did not require this file, review the turn. Consider terminal.credential_files and Hermes's read denylist for stores the agent should never see.
missing_evidence: Whether the read returned content is visible only through the tool status; the bytes are not recorded.
findings.attack_note: Refined per store: T1552.004 for private keys, T1555.001 for the macOS keychain, T1555.003 for browser stores.

findings.rule_name: Untrusted content followed by sensitive action
findings.title: [REPLAY] Untrusted fetch from 127.0.0.1 preceded secret.access
findings.observed: 1 untrusted-content event(s) (latest: web_extract fetch 127.0.0.1) then secret.access → /Users/demo/siemless-lab/.ssh/id_rsa.
findings.why: Instructions hidden in fetched content are the usual way an agent is steered into exactly this sequence.
findings.recommendation: Read the fetched page or file for embedded instructions. If the downstream action was not asked for by the user, treat the source as hostile and review what else happened in this turn.
missing_evidence: The content itself is not stored, so the injected text is not quoted here; the session transcript has it.
Causality is temporal: the action followed the fetch inside the window.
findings.attack_note: Attached to the *downstream* action, not to the fetch: reading a web page is not an attack.
